## Spatial analysis

::: {.cards}

::: {.card-et}
### Pedestrian casualties on London's roads
<p class="meta">2026 · Python, GeoPandas, OSMnx, PySAL, statsmodels, Leaflet</p>

I analysed every pedestrian casualty recorded by the police in Greater London from 2021 to 2025. I found the hotspots along the street network with network kernel density and Getis-Ord Gi*, used a negative binomial model to look at the built environment, and measured drive times to the major trauma centres. In the dashboard you can explore any place with the spotlight, play through the years, download the data as CSV and ask the AI assistant questions in plain English.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/london-pedestrian-safety/">Dashboard</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/london-pedestrian-safety">Code</a> <a href="posts/2026-10-athens-to-london/">Write-up</a></p>
:::


::: {.card-et}
### Pedestrian collisions in Athens
<p class="meta">MSc Geoinformatics, NTUA (2021), re-analysed in 2026 · Python, NetworkX, PySAL, statsmodels, mgwr, Leaflet</p>

I rebuilt my MSc thesis on 1,318 pedestrian collisions in Athens (2008–2017) as open code. I used network kernel density along the streets, emerging hotspots over the ten years, Local Moran's I, and walking distances to bars, schools, crossings and bus stops. The negative binomial model showed that collisions follow how busy a place is, and once that is taken into account, bars no longer explain them. GWR shows where each factor matters. The emergency services dashboard has the hospital duty rota (εφημερίες), and you can click anywhere to see the nearest hospitals, police and fire stations.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/athens-pedestrian-safety/">Dashboard</a> <a href="https://etymo.co.uk/athens-pedestrian-safety/story.html">Story</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/athens-pedestrian-safety">Code</a></p>
:::

::: {.card-et}
### Last orders? The UK drawn with its pubs
<p class="meta">2026 · Python, GeoPandas, SciPy, Leaflet · FSA and ONS open data</p>

A fun data story. I downloaded the food hygiene register and drew all 38,000 pubs and bars as dots, without any coastline or roads, and the UK still shows up. Then I checked whether COVID made a difference and found that the big wave of closures came in 2008, and that it was mostly the small pubs that closed. I also looked at the most common pub names, the streets that are basically a pub crawl and the furthest you can get from a pint. You can check how pubby your postcode is too.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/uk-pubs/">Story</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/uk-pubs">Code</a> <a href="posts/2026-10-uk-pubs/">Write-up</a></p>
:::

::: {.card-et}
### Can you draw Greece with tavernas?
<p class="meta">2026 · Python, GeoPandas, Leaflet · OpenStreetMap and ELSTAT</p>

The Greek follow-up to the pubs. Greece has no register like the UK, so I used OpenStreetMap and drew 6,300 tavernas, kafeneia and ouzeri as dots. When I compared it with ELSTAT, the map turned out to have less than half of the places, and much fewer in the north than on the islands. I also looked at how bars and cafés changed since the crisis and at the most common taverna names (Panorama wins, there's no Red Lion).

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/greek-tavernas/">Story</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/greek-tavernas">Code</a> <a href="posts/2026-10-greek-tavernas/">Write-up</a></p>
:::

## Planning and geospatial tools

::: {.cards}

::: {.card-et}
### Article 4 and constraints checker, Kingston
<p class="meta">Web tool · JavaScript, Leaflet, Planning Data API, proj4</p>

I built this to help with Local Land Charges searches at the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames. You can check one property by address, postcode or grid reference, or upload a CSV to check hundreds at once. Each location is checked through the government's Planning Data service for Article 4 directions, conservation areas, listed buildings, tree preservation, green belt, flood zones and SSSIs. Anything within 10, 25 or 50 m of a boundary is flagged as borderline. Article 4 results are also checked against Kingston's own boundaries, and the tool still works offline if the service is down.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/Article4Kingston/">Open the checker</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/Article4Kingston">Code</a></p>
:::

::: {.card-et}
### Retrofit planning checker
<p class="meta">Web tool · JavaScript, Leaflet, Planning Data API, HM Land Registry INSPIRE</p>

Can this home have a heat pump, solar panels or insulation without planning permission? You enter an address, postcode or grid reference anywhere in England. For each common energy improvement, the checker tells you if it's usually permitted development, allowed with limits, needs prior approval, or needs planning permission or listed building consent, and links to the rule. It checks listed buildings, conservation areas, Article 4 directions, protected trees, flood zones and more across the whole Land Registry plot, and takes the type of home into account. There's also a batch mode for whole retrofit programmes. If a council hasn't published its data, the checker says "check with the council", so it never says "allowed" when it can't know.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/RetrofitChecker/">Open the checker</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/RetrofitChecker">Code</a></p>
:::

::: {.card-et}
### Planning Data Tracker
<p class="meta">Web tool and weekly pipeline · Python, GitHub Actions, Leaflet</p>

While building the Kingston checker, I found 113 Article 4 areas that didn't link to their directions. That made me realise planning tools can only answer from what councils publish, so "no tree preservation order" might really mean "we don't know". This tracker shows, for all 337 local planning authorities in England, which of 10 council datasets have records in their area, from Article 4 and conservation areas to brownfield land and local green spaces. It also flags data problems with Article 4 directions. It updates every week, and you can re-check any council live.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/PlanningDataTracker/">Open the tracker</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/PlanningDataTracker">Code</a></p>
:::

::: {.card-et}
### Takeaways near schools
<p class="meta">Web tool · JavaScript, Leaflet, FSA and DfE open data</p>

Many councils restrict new hot-food takeaways near schools. For any council in England, this maps every open school with a zone around it (200 to 800 m, you choose), every takeaway from the food hygiene data, and which schools have the most takeaways nearby. You can choose which school phases count, check if a proposed site falls inside a zone and download the results as CSV. I've listed the limits too: distances are straight lines, and food hygiene categories are not the same as planning use classes.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/TakeawaysNearSchools/">Open the tool</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/TakeawaysNearSchools">Code</a></p>
:::

## Remote sensing

::: {.cards}

::: {.card-et}
### Green Change Monitor
<p class="meta">Web tool · Sentinel-2, NDVI, Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFFs, geotiff.js</p>

Where were trees and green space lost or gained? You pick an area and two years, and it maps where vegetation was lost or gained using free Sentinel-2 imagery. It all runs in the browser. It finds the clearest images, masks the clouds, makes a cloud-free greenness map for each year and compares them. In England, it flags changes inside conservation areas and tree preservation areas, so planning and enforcement teams know where to look first. You can download the results as GeoJSON or CSV. It shows you where to look, but it isn't evidence on its own.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/GreenChangeMonitor/">Open the monitor</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/GreenChangeMonitor">Code</a></p>
:::

## Cartography

::: {.cards}

::: {.card-et}
### Andros island web map
<p class="meta">2019 MSc cartography project, rebuilt 2026 · Python, GeoPandas, rasterio, Leaflet</p>

I made an interactive map of the whole island of Andros in a single web page, from my own 2019 data and 13 m terrain model. It has relief shading and you can search for villages, beaches, churches and monuments. Click anywhere to get the elevation and the coordinates in WGS84 and Greek Grid (ΕΓΣΑ87), or draw a route to see its elevation profile. You can also switch on OpenStreetMap layers for public services, springs and walking trails. It doesn't need a map server, so a small municipality could host it easily.

<p class="links"><a href="https://etymo.co.uk/AndrosWebMap/">Open the map</a> <a href="https://github.com/eritrouib/AndrosWebMap">Code</a> <a href="posts/2026-10-andros-web-map/">Write-up</a></p>
:::

## Reality Checks

Ten small calculators based on research, so you can try the evidence on yourself. They're all in one place at **[realitychecks.app](https://realitychecks.app)**. Each one explains what it can and can't tell you: the results are population averages, and they can't predict what will happen to you personally.
